structure.note: Class A and Class B have one vote per share and identical economic rights, but vote separately to elect directors: while Class B is between 25% and 87.5% of all common shares, Class A elects 75% of the board (nine of twelve nominees in 2025). Swoosh, LLC holds 78.5% of Class A. Phil Knight has no voting rights over Swoosh; the 10-K says his son Travis Knight, a director, 'has a significant role in the management of the Class A Common Stock owned by Swoosh, LLC.' 'controlled' is false: no person or entity holds over 50% of all votes (on matters other than director elections the classes vote together, one vote per share, and Knight entities hold well under half), and neither filing calls Nike a controlled company. Through Class A, however, Knight entities effectively decide most board seats.

notes: Fiscal year ended May 31, 2025 (Nike's fiscal 2025; matches data.js fy 'May 2025'). Documents read on sec.gov: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0000320187-25-000047) and 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0000320187-25-000048), ownership as of June 30, 2025. OWNERSHIP: the proxy states percentages only per class, and its Class B column assumes each holder's Class A has been converted, so no figure in the table is a share of all common stock. Phil Knight's economic share is therefore given only as leader.derived (2.43%). The family field holds Swoosh, LLC with pctEconomic null: the proxy gives it 78.5% of Class A and 16.0% of Class B on an as-converted basis, but no share of all common stock, and recomputing it is not allowed. The proxy says the table 'contains substantial duplications in the numbers of shares and percentages of Class A and Class B Stock shown for Swoosh, LLC, Philip Knight, and the Travis A. Knight 2009 Irrevocable Trust II'. Philip Knight's line excludes Swoosh's shares, and Travis Knight disclaims Swoosh's shares. The Travis A. Knight 2009 Irrevocable Trust II (27,181,369 Class A, 9.4% of Class A) is another Knight family holder; it is not added to the family figure or listed as a holder, to avoid summing or double counting. LARGEST HOLDERS left empty on purpose: The Vanguard Group (109,539,710 shares, 9.0% of Class B, per a 13G/A as of December 29, 2023) and BlackRock (89,773,424 shares, 7.3% of Class B, per a 13G/A as of December 31, 2023) are stated only as percentages of Class B, not of all shares. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow line covers common and preferred together. Nike's only preferred stock is 300,000 redeemable preferred shares held by Sojitz, so the line is effectively common dividends, and XBRL tags it PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock. BUYBACKS: cash paid ($2,985 million). The equity statement shows $2,955 million of shares repurchased and retired, which is not used. GEOGRAPHY: rows copied from the segment note. The 'Corporate' column (revenues of -$97 million, mainly foreign-currency hedge gains and losses) is omitted because a segment value cannot be negative, so the segments sum to $46.41 billion against the reported total of $46.31 billion. Global Brand Divisions (licensing) and Converse are not geographic. Item 1 of the 10-K says NIKE Brand and Converse sales in the United States were about 43% of total revenues in fiscal 2025.
